subject: Hosted latency qualification — data ask & runbook proposals
messages:
From: Rafael Mendes <rafael_mendes@redwood.inference>
To: Sara Lim <sara@brightpathlabs.com>, ops+latency@brightpathlabs.com
Cc: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.inference>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.inference>
Date: Thu, 17 Sep 2026 15:10:00 -0700
Subject: Hosted latency qualification — data ask & runbook proposals

Hi Sara — thanks again for the call earlier. Quick recap and concrete asks so we can scope a short qualification run against our hosted API (aiming to compare end-to-end p95/p99 vs your current provider).

Summary from the call:
- BrightPath target: p95 <= 250ms, p99 <= 450ms for single-turn inference for the guidance model under typical traffic.
- Typical concurrency: ~200 concurrent active users during peak 1-hour window; sustained throughput ~800 req/min; occasional bursts to 2,400 req/min for 3–7 minutes.
- Streaming: roughly 12% of requests use streaming with average token counts similar to non-streaming but require sub-100ms initial token latency.
- Success criteria: measured p95/p99 E2E (client -> Redwood hosted API -> model -> response) across matched traffic profile; request-level success rate >= 99.8%.

Concrete asks (what we need from you to run a comparable qualification):
1) Traffic sample: a 1-hour CSV sample (timestamp, endpoint, payload-size-approx, user-session-id) that represents your typical peak. Attached is a template (postcall-traffic-sample.csv) — can you populate with one recent peak hour?
2) Provider report: if you have a recent 1-hour latency report from your current provider (p50/p95/p99, concurrency timeline, error rates), please attach — you mentioned you could share an anonymized export.
3) Test account & allowlist: confirm an IP range or CIDR for us to allowlist and whether you prefer a short-lived API key for the lab or token-based test traffic.
4) Measurement clarifications: confirm whether your p95/p99 targets are measured client-side (including network) or server-side only. We will match whichever you use but need that detail to compare apples-to-apples.

Proposed next steps from our side:
- We’ll provision a short-lived hosted test endpoint and run a matched traffic replay for the sample you provide (1–2 hours).
- Deliverables: time-series of p50/p95/p99, request-level traces for high-tail requests, and a small actionability doc (batching/streaming tuning and concurrency knobs) with cost delta estimates.
- Schedule a 60-minute deep-dive to walk through results (I proposed slots below).

Suggested meeting slots (PST):
- Fri 18 Sep 2026 — 09:00–10:00 or 13:30–14:30
- Mon 21 Sep 2026 — 11:00–12:00

If you can send the CSV and the provider report today or tomorrow we can run the first replay Monday.

Thanks — Rafael
Rafael Mendes

Subject: Re: Hosted latency qualification — data ask & runbook proposals

Thanks Rafael — appreciate the clear asks. See answers inline: 

- We can export the 1-hour sample from last Wed at peak (I attached the anonymized CSV).
- Attaching current-provider-latency-report.pdf — it includes client-side p50/p95/p99 and a concurrency timeline for that hour. Note: our monitoring side measures p95/p99 from the app host (so includes client network and some infra hops).
- For the lab, we prefer a short-lived API key and will provide a test VPC egress IP range to allowlist.

We should also flag a peculiarity: our streaming traffic has an initial token time objective of <120ms rather than <100ms — we can tolerate 120ms if that's helpful.

I'll check with ops and send the CSV + PDF within the hour. Best,
Sara

sara@brightpathlabs.com

Date: Fri, 18 Sep 2026 08:25:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Hosted latency qualification — data ask & runbook proposals

Perfect — thanks for the quick turn. A couple quick clarifications before we kick off the replay: 

1) Measurement parity: since your report is client-side, we'll run the Redwood-hosted test with a small synthetic client in the same region and capture both client-side and server-side perspectives so we can align metrics.
2) Streaming SLAs: we can target initial token <120ms to match your tolerance; please confirm if that should be considered a pass/fail threshold or an advisory target.
3) Auth / allowlist: once we have the CIDR and the account to issue a short-lived key against, we'll generate the test endpoint and share the key over the HubSpot secure note.

Proposed lab run schedule: Mon 21 Sep 2026 10:00–12:00 PST. If that works, we'll reserve infra and share a lightweight runbook (how we replay the events, how we throttle bursts, and what traces we'll collect).

Karthik — can you stand up the replay job and a lightweight tracing dashboard for the run? We'll keep the initial run conservative (2 concurrent replay workers) then scale to the target traffic.

Sara — we’ll mark initial token <120ms as a pass/fail metric for streaming for the first run (we can always tighten in a follow-up).

Thanks — Rafael
